translation_notes: 7 isolated .add() calls across 3 different graphs (onto, align, clean_kb) inside two loops plus one rewrite loop. Each becomes @graph <var> + +{ }, re-declaring @graph whenever the site switches graph (block-scope allows redeclaring @graph mid-suite, takes effect from that line to the end of the enclosing suite per declarations.md).

Two of onto's three .add() calls on the same iteration (rdf:type and rdfs:domain) share the subject priv_prop unconditionally, so they were merged into one +{ s p1 o1 ; p2 o2 } (add_run_shared_subject shape) rather than kept as two separate +{ } -- this does not fit add_isolated's own definition but is the honest, most-specific translation for that pair. The third (rdfs:range) is conditional on `not is_obj_prop` and stays a separate +{ }: `;` cannot express a conditionally-included predicate-object pair without restructuring, which is forbidden.
onto.add(...) and align.add(...) never share a subject VALUE across graphs (same Python variable, different target graph), so no further merging applies there.

Function reads/writes graphs via 6 file-path arguments, not a Graph parameter: fixture.ttl's single-file convention did not fit, so driver.py stages 3 read-only input fixtures (fixture_kb.nt, fixture_ontology.ttl, fixture_alignment.ttl) and one fresh temp dir of output paths per side, then compares the 3 written files by RDF isomorphism -- same oracle (corpus/405), adapted for a file-based entry point instead of a graph-argument one.
Verified the fixture is not a hollow green: corrupting one predicate in translated.ldpy (rdfs:domain -> rdfs:seeAlso) flips the check to FAIL on ontology_expanded.

Credit correction (2026-11-02, corpus/403 defect 3): dropped `@prefix` for `rdf:`, `xsd:`, declared by the mechanical draft but never used as a term in the translated region (and not among the bindings the original sets on its graph); `rdfeval check` stays OK.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: `Graph(); g.parse(...)` becomes `Graph().parse(...)` (parse returns the graph); the `;`-joined bind calls are one per line (same calls); the str() around terms in the noise filter is dropped (rdflib terms are str); the removal loop is `kb -= triples_to_remove`; the two `align.triples((None, P, None))` comprehensions use subject_objects(P); the startswith tests use the Namespaces themselves (`p_str.startswith((DBO, DBP))`, `startswith(DBR)`); prop_name is inlined; the rdf:type and rdfs:domain adds of a new property are one `onto += [...]`; URIRef(p_str)/URIRef(node_str) are p/node themselves; the set union is `{*kb.subjects(), *kb.objects()}`; the three new_s/new_p/new_o variables are inlined in the add. The eleven prints, the phase comments and translation_map are kept: replacing translation_map by the two aligned dictionaries would translate terms the original leaves alone.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph onto` once after the parses (onto is never reassigned), the align adds with the call suffix (align) instead of re-declaring @graph twice, `@graph as clean_kb` for the rewritten graph; the two subject_objects reads become `m{ ?s owl:equivalentProperty ?o }(align)` and `m{ ?s owl:sameAs ?o }(align)` (m{ } iterates graph.triples in the same order, so the last-wins dict is the same), a little longer than the call with a prefixed name but the most specific construction; the rdf:type/rdfs:domain pair is one +{ } with `;`, the class chosen by `{owl:ObjectProperty if is_obj_prop else owl:DatatypeProperty}`.
No exception to the symmetry rule. The region is dominated by prints, file I/O and dictionary bookkeeping that neither the rereading nor the notation touches (care 0.90, notation 0.96).
